query: How can support teams reduce ticket resolution time?

per_column.name: issue_type_category
per_column.rationale: Gives a strong grouping axis to compare resolution times across issue kinds. Categorizations across the samples (billing_error, auth_failure, feature_request, bug_functional) are sound readings of the source text. CS-0003 as 'performance_degradation' is defensible for a 502 outage though arguably an integration/infra failure; still warranted.

per_column.name: has_blocker_or_dependency
per_column.rationale: Dependency/blocker status is highly relevant to resolution time and offers a genuine modeling axis. Values are mostly warranted; 'not_present' for the enhancement row and 'requires_customer_action' for the billing case (customer paid, wants corrected invoice) are reasonable, though the billing case leans more toward internal action. Minor interpretive stretch, not invention.

per_column.name: urgency_indicator
per_column.rationale: Urgency is useful for prioritization analysis but partly overlaps with the existing 'priority' column, slightly reducing new leverage. Values are mostly grounded (critical_outage for the 502, enhancement_only for the pin request). 'revenue_at_risk' for a 49-dollar duplicate line item is a mild overreach given the small dollar amount, but the finance-close deadline offers some basis.

per_column.name: technical_root_cause_domain
per_column.rationale: Root-cause domain is a valuable axis for targeting systemic fixes. However several values assert causes the text does not establish. CS-0001 labeled 'data_corruption' when the text describes a duplicate line item (billing logic, not corruption). CS-0003 labeled 'infrastructure_scaling' though the text only states a 502 with no scaling evidence. CS-0005 'schema_validation' for a BOM character is a stretch. These are confident specifics where the text is silent about the true cause.

per_column.name: resolution_action_required
per_column.rationale: Directly actionable for the query about reducing resolution time by routing tickets correctly. Most values are reasonable (bug_fix for the BOM issue, platform escalation for the outage). CS-0001 as 'direct_support_configuration' is defensible, and CS-0002 'engineering_bug_fix' is a plausible inference. Some assignments over-specify a resolution path the text does not confirm, but they are warranted inferences overall.

judge.rationale: All five columns add genuine grouping/comparison/routing axes relevant to reducing ticket resolution time, with only mild redundancy between 'urgency_indicator' and the existing 'priority'. Groundedness is generally sound for categorization columns, but 'technical_root_cause_domain' notably asserts specific root causes the source text does not support (data_corruption for a billing duplicate, infrastructure_scaling for a bare 502), and 'resolution_action_required' occasionally over-specifies. 'not_present' values on silent rows are correct and not penalized.
